scope: SaaS web only; legacy JSON auth remains when the browser header is absent

browser_request.origin: exact configured BASE_URL origin; one Origin header; no query

pair_response.access_token_alias: retained only if already present; equal to token

ack_without_pair: existing body unchanged; successful credential revocation can expire refresh cookie

refresh.proof: cookie only; no body or Bearer fallback

body.refresh_token: one legacy RAM proof, bounded at 8192

logout.proof: cookie only; never general resource authority

response.server_confirmed: true only after confirmed existing revocation; false for absent or invalid cookie

invalid_origin.effect: no auth/provider I/O; no refresh cookie mutation (existing CSRF cookie remains independent)

errors.uncertainty: no automatic write replay, adoption, or confirmed revocation claim

cookie.Secure: true for HTTPS; HTTP only nonproduction loopback
cookie.expiry: existing verified refresh expiry; no extension beyond minted proof

browser_coordination.lock_scope: all cookie-capable operations through full response processing
browser_coordination.unsupported_locks: fail closed without authenticated I/O or credential Storage fallback
browser_coordination.cross_tab: invalidate RAM and sensitive DOM; do not adopt changed identity
browser_coordination.legacy: read once into RAM, immediately remove credential and metadata keys from localStorage/sessionStorage; migrate only through dedicated endpoint
browser_coordination.public_recovery: fragment proof in RAM with credentials omit; no authenticated bootstrap

resource_authority: unchanged access Bearer and persisted identity/version/RBAC/tenant/MFA checks; cookie alone cannot read private resources
validation_status: contract agreed; implementation and independent integration gates pending
